theorem.assumptions: A is the calibrated positive-definite target capacitance and E is any positive-semidefinite sum of unresolved static parasitic capacitances
theorem.tightness: equality is reached when E is rank one and aligned with the minimum-eigenvalue eigenvector of A

decision.supersededRandomOrientationHeadline: the 10-ppm random-orientation target is not an adversarial guarantee
decision.jointPacketTarget: use at most 8 ppm total unresolved low-frequency PSD parasitic norm for the current seven-frequency joint-fit claim
decision.everyFrequencyTarget: use at most 3.9 ppm if one-percent inverse agreement is claimed independently at every measured frequency
decision.multipleModes: the bound covers any coherent sum of passive static parasitic modes when eta is computed from the total PSD perturbation norm
decision.measurementRule: a resolved parasitic may exceed these limits only if it is included in the fitted model and passes new held-out frequency and drive tests

epistemicStatus.theorem: the PSD inverse-perturbation bound and its soft-mode rank-one saturation
epistemicStatus.conditionalApplication: the RLC correction assumes Q=30, the recorded frequency grid, a correctly calibrated global target scale and below-pole positive extracted capacitance
epistemicStatus.notEstablished: the bound covers indefinite de-embedding errors, active/nonreciprocal parasitics or dissipative model mismatch

established: the soft Gram mode makes the parasitic limit condition-number controlled; 8 ppm is a conservative rounded joint-packet target covering arbitrary passive PSD alignment and multiple coherent modes under the declared RLC band model
boundary: The theorem controls additive positive-semidefinite capacitance after scale calibration. It does not bound indefinite calibration error, complex dissipative admittance or poles inside the band, which must be rejected or modeled separately.
